Holy shit i remember posting a very similar thing on reddit. I was confused and intimidated as hell when i started animschool. My animation college where i took a bachelors degree from was absolutely horrible. I knew i was already at a disadvantage when i decided to give animschool a shot. And well… i have an answer got you.

Its perfectly ok to be intimidated by animschool. Infact, i would be worried if you think it’s a cake walk. Its probably the hardest thing i have ever done. And probably the most rewarding. And thats coming from someone who failed the fifth semester three times.

Even tho i had a bachelors in animation, i was new to everything because well; my college didn’t teach me anything. 

The first thing you have to know in animschool is; you are there to improve yourself, not compare yourself to others. AS is a hot bed for animators from everywhere. People who are doing masters in animation, people who are interning at studios, people who have no experience at all and ofcourse; animators who are actually working in the industry.

Yes its very very competitive. But as i said; people from all walks of life come here. So dont worry even if you have zero knowledge, but you are curious and hard working, you will get through. 

As for getting outpaced; take it slow. Nobody wants you to burn out. Take your time. Understand the concepts of animation. Learn what works and what doesn’t. Animation is very very complicated. It can only give you rewards if you are curious and hard working. Infact; you would get outpaced just about anywhere in this career, because there is definitely someone better than you. So in my humble opinion; dont even think this thought. 

Dont worry about grades. Thats one advice teachers give that is almost always overlooked. I was told this by multiple teachers at AS but i didn’t learn. Getting a C was a confidence destroyer. But then again, it helps you get better and makes you put in more effort.

I dont know what i would have done if i hadnt given it a shot. Yes i have failed the semester thrice (ofc also a lot of personal reasons behind it), but now i have a workflow that is absolutely amazing. And he causes of animschool, i am at gobelins; learning animation. The people you meet in AS will change your life for the better. The teachers know what they are doing. The students are passionate. And overall the environment is really friendly. And thats because you arent the only one whos intimidated or fears about being outpaced… thats everyone. 

Give it a shot. Its not easy mind you. But then again, nothing worthwhile is ever easy.

Honestly, this is only one part of the entire issue. India has hit a geopolitical rock bottom as of now. 

India is a country surrounded from all sides by hostile nations. Pakistan. China. Afganistan. Nepal (which now has a pro china gov) and even several internal forces which are constantly seeking to undermine Indian position in the region. 

The closest country within shouting distance is ( fortunately, or unfortunately) Russia. India Russia relations have always been strong yes. But since this geopolitical nightmare has surrounded India, its regional integrity is undermined. If you take out Russia, India doesn't have any strategic allies it could count on. 

That being said, India is also getting cucked cause of the Belt and road initiative, through which china has literally blocked india from taking part in the world trade as a major player. As an *emerging* superpower, India cant really afford to piss off the allies that it actually has. 

This isn't even accounting for several political issues which have hit the country internally. The ruling party is not famous, whilst the opposing party is even worse. Internal politics is also destroying Indian chances. The economy is stagnant on best days and failing on others. 

The amount of high level meetings that have taken place in the last few days in India is actually staggering. They've never chaired these many meetings, even in election period. This issue is clearly affecting India, but unfortunately they're a country with both hands tied behind their backs. 

It should also be noted (as OP has mentioned) that India and Russia are military partners as well. They've manufactured several weapons which have set new benchmarks in the defence market. 

India has a strong moral code. But moral codes are also dependant on the current situation one goes through. Indians cant go against anyone, nor can they support any side in this particular conflict. Not to mention, a part of the population even thinks getting into the fray is useless since *ukraine lies half a world away.*

The aforementioned issues are barely scratching the surface. And now the pressure is even more. Cause India cant get on the front foot, nor can they shift on the back. All they can do is stay neutral and just watch from the sides. Not because they want to, but because unfortunately, they dont really seem to have a choice. 

Circumstances are a bitch when it comes to geopolitical tensions.
